title: Probability in Finance - Statistics For The Trading Floor
reason: 为什么好决策也会有坏结果：期望值、大数定律和「结果论」，是理解回测与风险的思维基础。

notes.summary: 概率是量化金融的地基，但现实中人们习惯用「对/错」评判预测，而不是看背后的概率与过程。视频用 Nate Silver 的 2016 年预测、新冠死亡人数预测、扑克玩家 Annie Duke 的「resulting」概念说明：好决策也会有坏结果，应当按概率与过程评价决策，而不是只看单次结果。
keyPoints: 预测应该表达为区间与置信度（如「95% 把握在 55 万–85 万之间」），而不是单一数字。
结果论（resulting）：只看单次结果评判决策，会把运气误当成技能。
独立事件的联合概率可以相乘（两枚硬币都正面 = 25%），但相依事件（连续下雨）不能这样算。
期望值 = Σ（各情形概率 × 对应收益）；估值、保险、信贷、期权定价都建立在期望值/概率之上。
大数定律：重复次数越多，平均结果越接近期望值；负期望值的游戏（如期望 0.7 美元、售价 1 美元的彩票）买得越多越必然亏钱。
概率常被忽视，是因为人们想要「确定性带来的安慰」，而不是不确定的真实数字。

glossary.def: 衡量不确定事件发生可能性的数值。
各结果概率与对应收益乘积之和。

glossary.term: Law of large numbers（大数定律）
glossary.def: 重复试验越多，样本平均越接近期望值。
一个事件的发生不影响另一个事件的概率。
仅凭单次结果来评价决策好坏的认知偏误（Annie Duke 用语）。
把预测的未来现金流按含风险的折现率折算为现值。

further: 视频作者的书《Statistics for the Trading Floor》

transcript.text: An event can be extremely likely and not happen, or an event can be extremely unlikely and still happen. This is an idea that many people find confusing. In today's video, we'll be discussing probability and why it's important for investors to have a good understanding of how it works. Probability is the study of events and outcomes that involve an element of uncertainty. Rolling a dice, for example, involves uncertainty, as does investing in the stock market. Rolling two dice at the same time has an uncertain outcome, but some outcomes are more likely than others, and the likelihood of the different outcomes can actually be quantified.
transcript.zh: 一个事件可能极有可能却没发生，也可能极不可能却发生了——很多人觉得这很困惑。本视频讲概率，以及为什么投资者需要真正理解它。概率研究带有不确定性的事件与结果：掷骰子、投资股市都有不确定性；同时掷两颗骰子结果不确定，但有些结果更可能，这种可能性可以被量化。

transcript.text: While most people do understand probability, in the real world few actually seem to believe in it. People understand that certain outcomes are rare and that the best you can do is to make decisions where the odds are generally in your favor. They understand that you can make a wise decision and end up being wrong or make a badly thought out decision and still end up right because that's just how luck and risk work. But almost nobody actually uses probability in the real world when judging things, in particular things like other people's successes. What people instead care about is, were you right or were you wrong? Probability is about nuance and gradation, but in the real world, people see things as being more black and white. If you said something will happen and it happens, you were right. If you said it will happen and it doesn't, you were wrong.
transcript.zh: 多数人理解概率，现实中却很少有人真正相信它。人们明白稀有结果存在、最佳做法是做「赔率有利」的决策，也明白明智的决策可能出错、拙劣的决策可能碰巧对。但几乎没人在评判事物（尤其是别人的成功）时使用概率——人们只关心「你对了还是错了」。概率讲究层次与程度，现实却非黑即白。

transcript.text: That's how people think, because it's easier to analyze outcomes than the thought process underlying a prediction. A famous example can be drawn from the 2016 U.S. presidential election, where American statistician Nate Silver calculated a 71% chance that Hillary Clinton would win the election that Donald Trump went on to win. Silver had been named one of the world's 100 most influential people by Time magazine in 2009 after his election forecasting system successfully predicted the outcomes in 49 out of the 50 states in the 2008 US presidential election. In the 2012 U.S. presidential election, his forecasting system correctly predicted the winner of all 50 states and the District of Columbia. Nonetheless, the main takeaway in 2016 was quite simply that Nate Silver was wrong.
transcript.zh: 这是因为分析结果比分析预测背后的思考过程容易。著名例子：2016 年美国大选，统计学家 Nate Silver 算出希拉里获胜概率 71%，结果特朗普赢了。Silver 此前因预测 2008 年 50 州中的 49 个、2012 年全部 50 州加华盛顿特区而入选《时代》百大影响力人物；可 2016 年人们的结论就是「Silver 错了」。

transcript.text: Great examples can be drawn from the 2020 coronavirus pandemic as well. News headlines say things like, experts predict 700,000 deaths by the end of July. What they should say is experts have a 95% confidence that the number of deaths by the end of July will be between 550,000 and 850,000 or something like that. It doesn't necessarily make a snappy headline, but that's actually what a prediction looks like.
transcript.zh: 2020 年新冠疫情也是好例子。新闻标题写「专家预测 7 月底将有 70 万人死亡」；更恰当的说法是「专家有 95% 的把握认为 7 月底死亡人数在 55 万到 85 万之间」。这不够吸睛，但这才是预测该有的样子。

transcript.text: With the original headline, if the number of deaths by the end of July turns out to be, say, 650,000, people will declare the experts wrong, even though it was pretty close. If the number turns out to be 900,000, they'll be called disastrously wrong, even though the forecasters knew there was a reasonable chance of that occurring. Misunderstanding probability happens a lot in investing too. Predictions that come true bring invitations to talk on CNBC.
transcript.zh: 按原来的标题，若实际是 65 万，人们会说专家错了，尽管已经很接近；若是 90 万，会被骂得一塌糊涂，尽管预测者知道有相当可能出现。投资中同样常见这种误解：预测成真的人被请上 CNBC，没成真的则被事后正确的人嘲笑。

transcript.text: Predictions that don't bring mockery from those who end up being right. Probability theory began in 17th century France, when the two great French mathematicians Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat corresponded over problems from games of chance. These types of problems continue to influence early researchers in establishing a mathematical theory of probability. Today, probability theory is a well-established branch of mathematics that's applicable in every area of scholarly activity, from physics to weather prediction to predicting the risks of new medical treatments.
transcript.zh: 概率论起源于 17 世纪法国，帕斯卡与费马通过通信讨论赌博问题。如今它是成熟的数学分支，应用于物理、天气预报、新疗法风险评估等各个领域。

transcript.text: Knowing the probability of getting heads when flipping a coin is 50%, the probability of flipping heads on two coins flipped at the same time is then 50% times 50%, or 25%. The four possible outcomes are heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads and tails-tails. Thus there is a one in four chance of flipping two heads, or 25% That calculation of course only works when the two events are independent of each other Looking at events like weather forecasts and questioning the likelihood of having two rainy days in a row recognizes that such events are different to coin flips. Rain yesterday might actually predict rain today because storms can last more than one day and of course because weather is seasonal. Probability turns up in all areas of finance. Probability allows financial
transcript.zh: 抛一枚硬币正面概率 50%，两枚同时抛都是正面则是 50%×50%=25%（四种结果 HH、HT、TH、TT，四分之一）。但这只在两事件相互独立时成立；「连续两天下雨」就不像抛硬币——昨天下雨可能预示今天下雨（风暴持续、天气有季节性）。概率出现在金融的各个领域。

transcript.text: professionals to calculate expected value. The expected value of an investment is simply the probabilities of the various outcomes multiplied by the various payoffs in the different scenarios. This is used everywhere from valuing a simple equity investment to pricing exotic derivatives. The insurance industry is almost entirely built on probability calculations, and an important component of credit is the probability a loan will be repaid.
transcript.zh: 概率让金融从业者能计算期望值：一项投资的期望值 = 各种结果的概率 × 各情形下的收益之和。从给简单股票估值到给奇异衍生品定价都在使用；保险业几乎完全建立在概率计算上；信贷的重要一环是贷款被偿还的概率。

transcript.text: In my book, Statistics for the Trading Floor, which is linked to in the description below, I work through all of the important probability calculations and how they can be applied to stock market analysis. As I mentioned earlier, good ideas as measured by probability can turn out badly and bad ideas can turn out well, at least in the short run. In probability theory, the law of large numbers is a theorem that describes the result of performing the same experiment a large number of times. According to the law, the average of the results obtained from a large number of trials should be close to the expected value and will tend to become closer as more trials are performed. While every lottery does have a winner, if a person buys thousands of tickets that have an expected value of 70 cents, and they pay a dollar for each of these tickets,
transcript.zh: 作者的书《Statistics for the Trading Floor》讲解了这些概率计算及其在股市分析中的应用。正如前面所说，从概率角度看好的想法短期内可能结果很差，坏想法可能结果很好。大数定律：把同一试验重复很多次，结果的平均值会接近期望值，试验越多越接近。例：一张彩票期望值 70 美分、售价 1 美元，如果买上千张……

transcript.text: it becomes a mathematical certainty that they will lose money. In her best-selling book, Thinking in Bets, I'll put an Amazon link to it in the description below, professional poker player Annie Duke explains how in the long run, the cumulative effect of being a little bit better at decision making by taking probability into account can have a huge effect on how our lives work out. Things like jobs and relocation decisions are bets. Sales negotiations and contracts are bets. Buying a house is a bet All decisions are bets on the future. They shouldn't be viewed as being right or wrong based on how they turn out. Duke explains in her book how professional poker players try to avoid the intellectual foible of what she calls resulting, which means looking at a single outcome as opposed to considering the broader spectrum of possibilities. When poker players win,
transcript.zh: ……就必然亏钱。Annie Duke 在畅销书《Thinking in Bets》里说：长期看，决策上只好一点点、把概率考虑进去，累积效应会极大地影响人生走向。工作、搬家、销售谈判、合同、买房都是赌注，所有决策都是对未来的下注，不该按结果判断对错。职业扑克玩家努力避免她所说的「resulting」——只看单一结果，而不考虑更广的可能性。

transcript.text: they must separate luck from process. If they can figure that out, they can improve their game and their future outcomes and understand what was attributable to skill and what was attributable to randomness. When a poker player or an investor loses after placing a smart bet, they should not be upset. This is an outcome that has to happen once in a while. Understanding what would have been the best move relative to the probabilities is what actually matters. Probability is central to almost all of the formulas that are used in quantitative finance. Possibly the most basic calculation that we do in finance involves projecting likely or probable cash flows and then discounting them at an appropriate discount rate that takes risk into account. This is the discounted cash flow model. Modeling stock prices over time and determining fair prices for financial
transcript.zh: 赢牌时必须把运气和过程区分开，这样才能改进，弄清哪些是技能、哪些是随机性；聪明下注却输了不必沮丧，这种结果本来就会偶尔出现，重要的是理解相对于概率什么才是最佳选择。概率是几乎所有量化金融公式的核心：例如预测可能的现金流，再用包含风险的折现率折现（DCF 模型）；给股价随时间建模、确定金融工具的公允价格同样深深依赖概率论……

transcript.text: instruments is once again heavily grounded in probability theory, and this is how we price options. The insurance industry is fairly obviously based almost entirely on probability. So, why does probability then get ignored? Well, a lot of what goes on in the financial world is an attempt to rid yourself of the painful reality of not knowing what's going to happen next. Someone who tells you that there's a certain chance of recession happening doesn't do much to get rid of that pain, and in fact they might just be adding to it.
transcript.zh: ……这也是期权定价的方式。保险业显然几乎完全建立在概率之上。那为什么概率常被忽视？因为金融世界里很多行为，是想摆脱「不知道接下来会发生什么」这种痛苦的现实。有人告诉你「有一定概率出现衰退」并不能消除痛苦，反而可能加剧它。

transcript.text: But someone who says there is definitely going to be a recession this year offers something to grab onto with both hands that feels like taking control of your future. When you realize that making people feel better is more appealing than giving people useful figures, you start to see why financial professionals often avoid using probability at all in their discussions. But hopefully you can see here how important probability is and how important it is to improve your way of thinking and to think in a more scientific manner and that using things like probability and statistics should improve your investing performance and hopefully your life outcomes in general. Anyhow, have a great day. Bye.
transcript.zh: 而「今年肯定会衰退」这种话给了你可以紧紧抓住的东西，让你感觉在掌控未来。当你意识到「让人感觉好」比「给出有用数字」更有吸引力，就明白金融从业者为何常常避免使用概率。希望你看到概率的重要性，用更科学的方式思考；用好概率和统计应能改善你的投资表现，乃至生活结果。

quiz.q: 视频认为一个好的预测应该怎样表达？
options: 给出一个确定的数字
给出区间和置信度，如 95% 把握在 55 万–85 万之间
只说「会涨」或「会跌」
不给数字，只给方向
quiz.explain: 预测本来就带不确定性，用区间 + 置信度才是「预测该有的样子」。

quiz.q: 两枚均匀硬币同时抛，都是正面的概率是？
quiz.explain: 两个独立事件概率相乘：50% × 50% = 25%（四种等可能结果中占一种）。

quiz.q: 为什么「连续两天下雨」不能简单用抛硬币的方法相乘？
options: 因为下雨概率太小
因为两天的天气不是独立事件，昨天下雨可能预示今天下雨
因为天气无法预测
因为需要用加法
quiz.explain: 相乘只适用于独立事件；天气有持续性和季节性。

options: 最大收益 − 最小收益
各结果概率乘以对应收益，再求和
平均价格除以标准差
收益率的中位数
quiz.explain: 期望值 = Σ（概率 × 收益）。

quiz.q: 一张彩票售价 1 美元、期望值 70 美分。一个人买了几千张，大数定律意味着？
options: 他很可能赚钱
几乎必然亏钱，平均每张亏约 30 美分
结果完全随机，无法判断
只要中过一次奖就不会亏
quiz.explain: 大数定律：试验越多，平均结果越接近期望值（−0.30 美元/张）。

quiz.q: Annie Duke 所说的「resulting」指的是？
options: 只看单一结果来评判决策好坏
把决策拆成多个步骤
永远选择风险最小的方案
根据历史平均做决策
quiz.explain: 结果论：把好结果等同于好决策，忽视了运气与概率。

quiz.q: Nate Silver 在 2016 年给出希拉里 71% 的获胜概率，结果特朗普赢了。按视频的观点，这说明？
options: 他的预测方法肯定是错的
29% 的事件本来就有可能发生，不能仅凭一次结果断定他错
概率论在选举中不适用
他应该只报出胜者
quiz.explain: 概率 71% 意味着另一方仍有约 29% 的机会；人们却只按「对/错」评判。
